title: Regional diversion and LTS coordinator for hosted API rollouts
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a resilient coordinator component and operator runbook to orchestrate hosted API releases across regions and LTS channels. This ticket covers design and implementation of a Regional Diversion Controller (RDC) and LTS Coordinator that together enforce SLO-aware staged traffic shifting (blue/green & canary), ensure KV/cache compatibility across model variants, and provide deterministic rollback/rollforward semantics for runtime-1.24 releases.

Problem statement:
- Current rollouts rely on a mix of ad-hoc scripts and region-specific handoffs; we have observed inconsistent drain timings, cascade error spikes during regional rollouts, and manual mistakes when pinning model versions to tenant routes.
- We need a single controller that understands LTS channels (stable, beta, nightly), per-region capacity and SLOs, and can execute deterministic diversion plans with automatic holdpoints based on telemetry.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
1) Implement RDC to coordinate blue/green and canary shifts across regions with SLO gates.
2) Integrate with LTS channel metadata so customers pinned to an LTS get predictable upgrades.
3) Provide safe defaults for canary size, ramp speed, and drain windows; expose overrides for Dedicated customers.
4) Ensure automated rollback on configurable failure predicates and provide audit/trace for each step.
5) Integrate console controls and telemetry dashboards for runbooks and on-call visibility.

Acceptance criteria:
- RDC can perform a regional canary that ramps 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with configurable delay and abort predicates.
- Holdpoints are triggered when any of: request_error_rate > 0.5% (5m), p95_latency increases > 40% vs baseline (5m), or token_throughput falls below expected.
- Rollback completes and drains traffic to previous model within SLA (default 3 minutes non-burst, up to configured drain).
- LTS Coordinator maps customer pins to model artifact hashes and guarantees atomic switch per region.
- KV cache version compatibility check runs pre-shift and can opt into cache-warm path or cache-invalidations.

Design notes:
- RDC will be a stateless controller with a single leader per arena (region or global depending on config) persisted in our orchestration DB. It emits plan events (PlanID) with ordered steps: Preflight -> CanaryEntry -> Ramp -> Verify -> Promote -> Cleanup. Each step has explicit timeout and retry policy.
- Use optimistic traffic weights in gateway (edge-tier) with a header X-RDC-Plan to trace requests back to PlanID.
- Preflight includes schema compatibility, KV cache compatibility test, and a small synthetic sample against the candidate model. Failure in preflight marks plan as aborted.
- We will implement SLO gate evaluation using our observability events stream (metrics and traces) with built-in comparators and a rolling baseline window.
- Rollback will be a reverse-plan operation with an expedited drain and optional trace capture for root-cause.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- New Grafana dashboard: grafana.redwood.ai/d/rdc/rdc-rollouts (placeholder) showing per-plan time series: plan_phase, canary_weight, p50/p95 latency, error rate, QPS, token/sec, cache_miss_rate, and rollout-caused-resource-spikes.
- Alerts: rdc-rollout-abort (pager if abort predicate met and plan is > 2m old), rdc-rollout-slow-drain (warn if drain > configured threshold).

API/Console changes:
- POST /v1/rollouts to create a plan (payload includes model_hash, target_regions, lts_channel, ramp_policy, abort_predicates).
- Console: Rollouts page with timeline, per-region status, and one-click abort/promote/rollback actions for authorized users.

Compatibility and edge cases:
- Stateful customers with per-tenant cache/prefixing will be defaulted to manual approval path; RDC will surface a preflight checklist for these tenants.
- If model artifact requires a schema change, LTS Coordinator will require an explicit compatibility flag and a migration plan.

Implementation plan (phases):
Phase 1 (spike, 2w): RDC prototype that can do a single-region canary using traffic weights and emits PlanIDs.
Phase 2 (3w): Add SLO gate evaluation, preflight checks, and automated rollback.
Phase 3 (3w): Multi-region coordination, LTS mapping, console + API integration, and runbook documentation.
Phase 4 (1w): Hardening, security review, QA stress tests, and on-call training.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Incorrect drain times cause request loss for long-lived connections. Mitigation: implement graceful socket drain and fallback to sticky-session pinning during rollout.
- Risk: KV cache invalidation amplifies latency on promote. Mitigation: staged cache-warm path and synthetic warm requests before traffic shift.
- Risk: Observability lag causing false aborts. Mitigation: combine metrics with short window and require two consecutive evaluation windows before abort.

Rollout runbook (draft):
1) Create plan via API or Console with description and rollback rationale.
2) System runs preflight checks; if OK, begin canary in primary region.
3) Wait for 'burn-in' (default 10 minutes) while monitoring predefined metrics.
4) If gates pass, continue ramps per policy. On abort, plan auto-rollbacks and notifies oncall.
5) After promotion, cleanup old artifacts and mark plan complete.

Open questions:
- Default canary sizes and ramp timing for different model sizes (L, XL, 8B vs 70B) — need SRE input.
- How to represent tenant-specific custom routing in the plan API without leaking config complexity to the console.

References and artifacts:
- Design sketch (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/RDC+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/1428
- Observability proto dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rdc-proto/rdc-proto
- Runbook draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1abcDEF-ghijk (internal)

Next steps:
- Complete Phase 1 spike and demo to SRE/PM by 2026-01-29.
- Schedule security review after Phase 2 completes.
- Prepare a lab environment to rehearse multi-region rollouts against synthetic traffic.
